        History

          What stood out, ranked evidence, not proof

          Ranked by how far each was from the same hour over the last 28 days. These were present; they are not proven causes. A family the record does not carry shows No data.

          How to read this
          • Percent. Each family is compared with the five-minute intervals of the same clock hour on the last 28 days. "Higher than 78%" means the value was above 78% of those intervals; about 50% is normal. Fuel is compared with its own monthly history instead.
          • Rank. Families are ordered by that percent, most unusual first. Fuel is placed after the others whenever another family is above 80%. A rank says what was unusual, not what set the price: evidence, not proof.
          • Context, not ranked. The price itself is shown for reference and never ranked.
          • Rules flags. Pricing flags at the interval (such as the price cap) are listed as set or not set and never scored. Congested elements at stations with no known region are counted apart and never linked.
          • Withheld facts. Facts a tab cannot use at the cutoff (5 minutes after the interval starts) are left out and counted: those known only later, and in Strict also those without evidence of when they were known.
          • Tabs. As known at the time: each market run is assumed available at the end of its interval. Strict: only facts with evidence of when they were known. Hindsight: everything, including facts recorded later.
